newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus sacks energy bosses after tender protests.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus sacks energy bosses after tender protests.

text.p: The Cyprus cabinet appointed a new board of directors of the state-run electricity authority on Friday after accusations of irregularities in a multi-million pound contract for a new power plant.
The nine-member board had been accused by parliamentarians of endorsing a tender for generators for 36 million pounds ($77.7 million) that ignored technical experts who favoured a lower bid.
Last week the electricity authority awarded the turbines and boilers contract to Austrian Energy and Environment. Their tender was 3 million pounds higher than that of an Anglo-French venture, GEC.
Government spokesman Yiannakis Cassoulides said an inquiry had been ordered into the endorsement of the tender. The contract, he said, has been frozen pending the inquiry.
The generators were to be used in a new power plant at Vassiliko on the southern coast of the island.

"If it is not completed in the time frame of 33 months from its commencement or before the summer of 1999 there will be great consequences on the economy and the living standards of Cypriots," Cassoulides said. ($=0.46 pounds)
